content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: move 2 cross-skilled agents to general, offer overtime to 12 general agents 19:30-20:00, plus chat deflection and IVR callback. Predicted 81.9% service level for 19:00-20:00 at ₹792.","why":"General is short of agents because of a sick wave: 9 absences against a usual 2.4. Call volume is normal (564 vs 568 forecast), so the fix is adding capacity, not managing demand. Doing nothing leaves the window at 68.6%, with general at 44.4%. The no-cost and low-cost options only reach 68.0–73.3%. R1 is the cheapest plan that clears the 80% target. It lifts general to 74.0%, keeps payments at 88.3% and cuts abandons from 10.5% to 5.0%. Diagnosis confidence is medium: recent on-phone counts from 13:45 don't match the detector's staffing figures.","trade_offs":["Cost: ₹792, against ₹252 for P3, which reaches only 73.3% and leaves general at 56.1%.","R2 (20 overtime offers, ₹1,332) gives a bigger margin: 87.5% overall, general 81.1%, abandons 3.9%. That costs ₹540 more than R1.","Overall service level clears the target, but general alone stays below 80% at 74.0%. Its customers still wait longer than payments customers.","Risk to payments is low: it holds at 88.3%. Moving a 3rd agent (P4) would drop payments to 84.4% and make things worse overall (68.0%).","R1 depends on overtime take-up. If fewer than 12 accept, the window will likely fall short of 80%."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptances before 19:30. If take-up is well short of 12, consider widening the offer toward R2. Also watch general queue service level and any further sent-home-unwell entries after the last one at 14:20. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
